newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU assembly slams EU disunity over China.
newsitem.headline: EU assembly slams EU disunity over China.

text.p: The European Parliament on Thursday added its voice to criticism of the European Union for failing to support a United Nations resolution attacking China for human rights violations.
"Ever since the massacre in Tiananmen Square in 1989, the EU has traditionally backed resolutions on China in the U.N. Human Rights Commission," the EU assembly said in a resolution.
The resolution deplored the absence this year of a common EU stance on China at the Human Rights Commission.
Denmark, the United States and human rights activists have condemned the EU's silence.
An attempt last week by Copenhagen to push for an EU- sponsored resolution collapsed when France said recent improvements by China on human rights suggested dialogue was better than confrontation.

The EU divisions -- coupled with Washington's delay in deciding to co-sponsor the resolution until after last week's visit to China by U.S. Vice President Al Gore -- makes it unlikely the resolution will be adopted.
China said last week it would sign the U.N. International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, but was silent on a similar pact on political freedoms.
Beijing's announcement was timed to coincide with a visit to China by French Defence Minister Charles Millon on Monday.
France hailed the move and said it hoped a EU ban on arms sales to China imposed after the 1989 Tiananmen Square crackdown could be lifted.
Human rights activists have linked this and an enormous contract for French-built Airbus aircraft to China as reasons for France's reluctance to approve the resolution.
The EU assembly appealed to EU leaders to keep up constant pressure on Beijing to respect human rights throughout China, Tibet, inner Mongolia and Eastern Turkestan.
The call echoed the parliament's earlier plea for constant EU vigilance over Beijing's actions in Hong Kong, which returns from British to Chinese rule on July 1.
